text:
Cody Glass has found a home in New Jersey, and the Devils have found a way to keep winning: they've taken eight of their last ten. Glass has points in four straight games (a goal and three assists), including both halves of the home-and-home sweep of Washington.

The sixth overall pick in 2017, one spot after Elias Pettersson, never became the scorer Vegas hoped for, but he's turned into a useful center. He has 2 goals and 6 points in 21 games on about 12 minutes a night. The goals are light for his chances (7.7% shooting against a usual rate near 14%), so a few more should come. The less flattering number: New Jersey's share of expected goals drops by about six points when he's on the ice compared with when he sits.

Last season was his best, with 19 goals and 1.8 wins by Evolving-Hockey's count, 67th among forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he plays: 59% of his shots came off the rush, and he exits his zone with possession 58% of the time, though he dumps the puck in more than he carries it. On a winning team, that's a depth center doing his job.
